findings: Add the November lifecycle and bank-debit warning and correct cancellation, tracing, IC+ and dated dispute language. Retain May as historical authority, keep the two-way stripe-refunds source/concept route, and preserve disputes and separate receipts navigation with November’s method-specific links.
conflicts: The May capture expressly says disputes and chargebacks are impossible for fully refunded credit card charges (old raw line 14); the November counterpart omits that sentence (new raw lines 13–17). Date the historical claim in source lines 21/70 and concept line 20, and preserve the separate partially refunded and pending-dispute paths. The omission alone does not establish changed policy.

Source and concept describe card refund cancellation too broadly and the bank-information flow too narrowly. Only some card refunds qualify for a short Dashboard window before reaching the customer, excluding charge reversals. The API or Dashboard can cancel applicable refunds while bank information is uncollected, and November's workflow names examples beyond bank transfers.

Source line 29 and concept line 28 generalize the 7-business-day and reversal conditions to all references. Both guides apply those particulars to ARN, which is conditional on partner support, and distinguish STAN/RRN fallbacks and selected local references.

Source line 25 and concept line 24 state lower IC+ network fees categorically. Both guides say reversals usually incur lower network fees and IC+ users might see a difference; refund itself might incur a fee and original processing fees are not returned.

Both captures use two timing anchors for return of failed refund funds: up to 30 days from the post date in failure handling and from the request in tracing. Do not turn the two sections into a single exact deadline. Both also say statement appearance depends on network/issuer and separately give approximate 5–10 business days for a refund credit.

The pending-refund dispute guidance is Stripe's recommendation to accept/challenge the dispute to avoid duplicate reimbursement, not a guarantee of duplicate credits. November separately warns of possible duplicate credits when a bank debit is proactively refunded concurrently with the customer's bank initiating a dispute.
